label: core_kappa2_route_VFVSAIKG

graph_scope.name: four-site-20^4-single-substitution
graph_scope.vertices: all 20^4 = 160000 four-letter genotypes over ACDEFGHIKLMNPQRSTVWY (no stop codon)
graph_scope.edges: two genotypes differing at exactly one of the four positions
graph_scope.not_claimed: nothing about sequence space beyond these four sites, nor about biology

source.note: intervals are core's kappa=2 model; r1=lower, r2=upper, delta=0 reproduces them exactly

interval_model.rule: lower=round(mean(r1,r2)*1e6)-eps, upper=round(mean(r1,r2)*1e6)+eps, eps=ceil(kappa*sd_bin/2*1e6); r_k = raw mu_k minus mean raw mu of stop-codon rows; all integers (1e-6 growth-rate units)

delta_status: ASSUMED sensitivity bound (delta): not a confidence interval; two replicates cannot support simultaneous 95% bounds across 159,129 variants
interval_rule: [min(r1,r2) - delta, max(r1,r2) + delta] on scaled exact integers
assumptions: A1 (interval containment): the true scaled growth value of every LISTED genotype lies in [min(r1,r2)-delta, max(r1,r2)+delta]. This is an assumption about the assay, not proved.
A2 (scope): genotypes not listed, including imputed or stop-containing ones, are UNKNOWN; the theorem never constrains them and no certificate relies on them except as members of S.
A3 (graph): only the declared four-site single-substitution graph; absence of a route here is not absence of a biological route.
limitations: delta is an assumed sensitivity bound, not a statistical confidence bound.
Python text->integer conversion is checked by evolve.proof.verify_against_source, not by Lean.
Growth in the E. coli selection assay is a proxy for function, not kcat/KM.
Fitness values are real measurements only at listed rows; this certificate is descriptive (full-data), not a prediction benchmark.
